Versions behind an emoji analysis, in one row

Source: R/emoji-provenance.R
emoji_provenance.Rd

emoji_provenance() reports every version an emoji result depends on: tidyEmoji itself, the Unicode emoji version of the catalogue it detects against and the date of that catalogue's data file, the size of the catalogue, the emoji package supplying the shortcodes, keywords and detection regex, and the bundled lexicons. It is meant to be pasted into a methods section or stored beside a result.

Usage

emoji_provenance()

Value

A one-row tibble with columns tidyEmoji, emoji_pkg, unicode_emoji, unicode_emoji_date (the date in the header of the catalogue's data file, a Date), n_emoji (rows of the reference table; see Details), sentiment_lexicon, emotion_lexicon and R.

Details

None of these are cosmetic. A glyph newer than the catalogue is not detected at all; a lexicon covers a few hundred of the thousands of emoji that exist; and "we analysed emoji sentiment" without a lexicon name is not a reproducible statement. See emoji_lexicons() for the lexicons in detail and emoji_unicode_version() for the Unicode version on its own.

The catalogue moved in 0.6.0, so results from 0.5.0 and 0.6.0 differ, and this row is how to tell which you have. The catalogue is now Unicode's emoji-test.txt rather than the table inside emoji, which takes it from Emoji 16.0 to 18.0 and makes 182 more emoji detectable. In the other direction, a skin-tone swatch standing alone and a regional-indicator pair that is no country stopped being emoji occurrences; emoji_summary() counts both. A corpus re-run under 0.6.0 can therefore report more emoji or fewer, and unicode_emoji is the column that says why.

n_emoji counts rows of the reference table, which are spellings, not distinct emoji. With the Emoji 18.0 catalogue it is 5244, and those 5244 rows carry only 3972 distinct code-point keys, because an emoji whose presentation can be selected appears both with and without U+FE0F. A methods section reporting "5244 emoji" therefore overstates the vocabulary by the 1272 duplicate spellings; length(unique(emoji_properties()$key)) is the count of distinct emoji, nine of which are the skin-tone and hair components, which are not emoji on their own. 212 of the 5244 spellings are not detectable in text as written under the default presentation (see emoji_sentiment_lexicon for why, and emoji_summary() for presentation = "any"). No emoji is lost to that: every one of the 3963 keys that is not a component is reachable through at least one detectable spelling. The two lexicon strings count their tables' rows the same way.

See also

emoji_unicode_version(), emoji_unicode_releases(), emoji_lexicons().

Examples

emoji_provenance()
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   tidyEmoji emoji_pkg unicode_emoji unicode_emoji_date n_emoji sentiment_lexicon
#>   <chr>     <chr>     <chr>         <date>               <int> <chr>            
#> 1 0.7.0     16.0.0    18.0          2026-04-30            5244 novak2015 (969 e…
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: emotion_lexicon <chr>, R <chr>
